interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is documented. Positive surgical margins is documented. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 28.44 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 22.75–34.13 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology revealed a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological stage pT3a, with positive surgical margins. The seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent. The report states, "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3), pathological stage pT3a. Extraprostatic extension was present; surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." This adverse finding of positive margins and extraprostatic extension is a significant prognostic factor. Countervailing findings include the absence of lymph node metastasis and non-invasion of the seminal vesicles. The preoperative PSA was 25. The biopsy identified Gleason 4+4 disease. Missing postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are critical unknowns that would revise the prognosis regarding biochemical recurrence. The pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, and missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding regional spread. Postoperative PSA and its trajectory are needed to assess biochemical recurrence risk.

nodal_contradiction: The pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, and missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding regional spread

Extraprostatic extension was present; surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." Biopsy findings showed Gleason 4+4. The pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, and missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding regional spread. The positive surgical margins and T3a extension represent adverse findings. Countervailing to this, the absence of lymph node metastasis and non-invasion of the seminal vesicles are reassuring. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, so biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would revise the prognosis.
